analysis.title: 2027 US rate forecast update
key_insights: CACIB expects the 2Y Treasury yield to rise toward 5.00% by mid-2027 (summary says high 4.00% area, Fig 3 shows 4.95% in Mar-27 and Jun-27) as the Fed completes its tightening cycle.
The 10Y Treasury yield is forecast at around 5.15% by H127 (Mar-27 in Fig 3), supported by resilient growth, elevated inflation, large Treasury financing needs and an elevated term premium.

House view is two more 25bp Fed hikes, in December and March, taking the upper bound of the Fed Funds rate to 4.50%. The bank argues the Fed can stop there if inflation evolves in line with its forecasts, while markets price a more aggressive cycle.

Labour market is resilient. October payrolls rose 165k, above expectations, and unemployment edged lower. Economists expect unemployment to average about 4.2% in 2027, which lets the Fed focus on inflation.

Inflation is hotter. October core CPI rose 0.3% MoM and 3-month annualised core accelerated to 3.75% from 3.41%. Strategists still expect headline in the mid-3% range through Q127 and core in a 2.7-2.9% range through early 2027.
The 2-10Y curve should flatten through H127, reaching its flattest around mid-2027 as the front end leads. It should stabilise in H227 and then steepen as inflation moderates and easing is priced.
Yields should fall in H227 with the front end leading the rally. The 10Y is seen back near 5.00% by late 2027 and early 2028, with further easing in early 2028 supporting lower yields.

Treasuries are caught between hot inflation that lifts yields and flight-to-quality demand that lowers them. An AI-related equity sell-off and fears of slower data center investment after the mid-term elections could help Treasuries.

Swap spreads are expected to widen modestly in 2027 with Treasuries outperforming swaps, helped by SLR and LCR reforms and ample Fed reserves. Coupon auction sizes are expected to be unchanged near term, then rise in H227 mainly in 2-7Y, favouring a steeper swap spread curve and wider 10Y-30Y spreads.
Upside risk to yields remains if inflation surprises, but already-high outright yields, improving inflation and equity-to-bond allocation shifts should limit the sell-off.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above expectations, supports the view that the labour market allows the Fed to focus on inflation.
Upside surprise that reinforces the Fed's cautious stance.
Acceleration supports hawkish pricing at the front end.
Stable labour market keeps inflation as the dominant policy driver.
Gradual improvement expected before moderating further.
Two 25bp hikes in December and March, then a hold.
Front end leads and the curve flattens.
Elevated term premium and supply keep long-end yields high.
Moderating inflation and easing focus pull yields lower.

trade_ideas.description: Swap spread curve steepener and Treasury outperformance vs swaps in 2027, including wider 10Y-30Y swap spreads
trade_ideas.rationale: Regulatory tailwinds (SLR, LCR), ample reserves and stable long-end supply support Treasuries versus swaps.
trade_ideas.risk: Additional front-end Treasury supply in H227 could weigh on shorter-maturity spreads.

risk_factors: Inflation upside surprises could push yields further up.
Larger Treasury supply in H227 could add upward pressure on yields.
An AI-related equity sell-off and slower data center investment could hurt growth.
Geopolitical escalation in Russia-Ukraine or US-Iran, including the Strait of Hormuz.
charts_described: Fig 3 table lists CACIB forecasts: 2Y Treasury 4.70% Dec-26, 4.95% Mar-27, 4.95% Jun-27, 4.50% Jun-28. 10Y Treasury 4.95% Dec-26, 5.15% Mar-27, 5.00% Dec-27.
vol_and_positioning: Markets price a more aggressive Fed tightening cycle than CACIB's two-hike view.
Risk-off demand for safe-haven assets is making 10Y Treasury yields near 5% increasingly attractive.
geopolitical: Russia-Ukraine peace talks are active but appear deeply stalled, with a wide gap between Russian demands and Ukrainian security requirements.
The June US-Iran MOU has not held and the Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint. De-escalation would lower energy prices and pressure front-end US rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot inflation data and heavy supply keep yields high, with the 2Y heading toward 5.00% and the 10Y toward 5.15% by H127.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk-off flight-to-quality flows, an AI-related equity sell-off and high outright yields attract buyers and limit the sell-off, with yields falling in H227.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation moderating so the Fed need not deliver the December and March hikes, or inflation surprising to the upside to push yields beyond forecasts.

theme_stances.key_argument: Hot inflation and further Fed hikes should push the 2Y toward 5.00% by mid-2027 and flatten the curve.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect the 2Y Treasury yield to rise towards 5.00% by mid-2027
